analysis.title: Year Six Of China's Housing Bust: Goldman Hikes Its Property Drag Estimate As Beijing Kills Off Presales
key_insights: Goldman's China economists (Yuting Yang, Lisheng Wang) now estimate property subtracts 1.8pp from China's 2026 real GDP growth, up from 1.7pp in 2025 and above their prior 1.5pp estimate. They had projected the drag to narrow this year.
Jan-Sep 2026 land sales revenue fell 28% YoY, new home starts fell 25% and property FAI fell 21%, all weaker than Goldman anticipated at the start of the year.
Most housing activity indicators are down 60-90% from 2020-21 peaks, with new home starts more than 80% below the top.

On August 28 Beijing announced a shift from presales to completed-home sales. Developers can presell only once the main structure has topped out, and mortgage proceeds go into supervised escrow until completion. Shenzhen was the last tier-1 city to publish detailed rules, on October 15, capping residential deposits at 3% of purchase price.

Nomura said deferring the release of funding until after completion 'effectively dismantles the financing function of presales'. Caixin reported land transaction volume across 70 major cities fell 36% in one week after the directive.
Goldman's property team expects 2025 to 2035 declines of 30% in new home starts, 46% in completions, 61% in property FAI, 70% in new home sales and more than 90% in residential land sales volume.
Goldman's macro baseline has land sales revenue, new home starts, new home sales and property FAI falling 20%, 20%, 10% and 17% in 2027, after drops of 30%, 22%, 8% and 20% in 2026.

Goldman replaced the NBS floor-space-under-construction series with its own model based on new home starts, because stuck or terminated projects still count in the official data. It also switched to the Ministry of Finance land revenue series because the NBS stopped publishing developer land purchases.
Government land revenue peaked above RMB 8 trillion in 2021, roughly halved by 2025, and is projected at about RMB 1 trillion by 2030.

Goldman estimates property was about 30% of GDP at the 2010-2021 peak, about 15% in 2025, and stabilizes near 8% from 2030. It expects the drag to narrow by about 0.5pp to 1.3pp in 2027 and largely fade by 2030.

Property is more than half of Chinese household assets. Goldman's rule of thumb is that RMB 1 of property value change moves annual household consumption by RMB 0.01. The total hit (direct plus wealth effect) was about 3.4pp at the 2024 trough, and the negative wealth effect peaked in 2024-25.

Goldman's baseline has nationwide existing home prices bottoming in 2030. Top-tier cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen may recover soon, while lower-tier cities with inventory overhang may keep declining for years.
Citi's Griffin Chan sees evidence of stabilizing and potentially rising prices in top cities. Shanghai became the first city with positive YoY secondary home price growth (+0.8% in September).

Goldman sees scope for a nationwide property tax expansion toward the end of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) or during the 16th (2031-35), given the projected land sales decline and local government financing pressure.

China's Q3 GDP growth bounced off three-year lows on exports offsetting weak consumers. September high-tech exports hit a record $147B (+63% YoY) and total exports rose 36%. China's September trade surpluses with Germany and France each rose more than 200% YoY, and Europe is planning further curbs.
Hartnett (BofA) calls 'China exports deflation' the biggest risk to global EPS. The CSI 300 is down 20% since June, and property investment is down 20% YoY.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman expects continued double-digit declines in starts, sales, FAI and land revenue through 2027 and falling nationwide existing home prices until 2030, with a smaller drag as the sector shrinks to about 8% of GDP.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects the drag to ease gradually as property shrinks from about 30% to about 8% of GDP, falling to 1.3pp in 2027 and largely fading by 2030. Top-tier cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen may see prices recover soon, and Citi sees stabilizing prices in top cities.
tension_points.bear_case: The drag widened in 2026 when Goldman expected it to narrow. The presale shift tightens developer funding, existing home prices bottom only in 2030, and lower-tier cities with inventory overhang may keep declining. Land revenue falls toward RMB 1 trillion by 2030, adding pressure on local governments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nationwide existing home prices failing to bottom by 2030, or further downward revisions to the drag estimate.

theme_stances.key_argument: Property drag on China GDP was revised up to 1.8pp for 2026 as activity data weakened and the presale shift tightens developer funding, though Goldman still expects it to fade by 2030.
theme_stances.evidence: downturn is deeper than previously anticipated

theme_stances.key_argument: Weak domestic demand pushes China to export its way out, with record exports raising the risk of global deflation and trade curbs.
